subject: general
question: Ashish has ₹1,218 with him. He divides it amongst his sons Arun and Mahesh and asks them to invest it at 10% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Arun and Mahesh got same amount after 11 and 12 years, respectively. How much (in ₹) did Ashish give to Mahesh?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When amounts are equal after **t₁** and **t₂** years, the ratio of shares is (1 + r/100)⁽t² − t¹⁾ : 1.

Ratio (Arun : Mahesh) = (1 + 10/100)⁽¹² − ¹¹⁾ : 1 = 11/10 : 1 = **11 : 10**.

Total units = 11 + 10 = 21 units → ₹1,218.

1 unit = ₹1,218 ÷ 21 = ₹58.

Mahesh's share = 10 units = 10 × 58 = ₹580.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹580.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/012d23267da0fadcec8abd59f6f41491cbc3cf468407337dfa8f6095ade70a06.png] 

**Given:**

Total Principal (P) = ₹1,218

Rate of Interest (r) = **10%** p.a. compounded annually.

Time for Arun (n₁) = **11 years** | Time for Mahesh (n₂) = **12 years**.

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P × (1 + r/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

Let Arun's share be **A** and Mahesh's share be **M**.

⇒ A + M = 1218

⇒ A × (1 + 10/100)¹¹ = M × (1 + 10/100)¹²

⇒ A × (1.1)¹¹ = M × (1.1)¹²

⇒ A = M × (1.1)¹² ÷ (1.1)¹¹

⇒ A = M × 1.1 = M × 11/10

⇒ A/M = 11/10

⇒ Total ratio sum = 11 + 10 = 21 units

⇒ 21 units = 1218

⇒ 1 unit = 1218 ÷ 21 = 58

⇒ Mahesh's share (M) = 10 units = 10 × 58

⇒ M = ₹580

**∴ The correct answer is ₹580.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The amount **A** after **n** years is given by A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, where **P** is the principal and **r** is the annual interest rate.

Equal Amounts Case

When two people receive the same amount at the same rate but for different times **t₁** and **t₂**, the ratio of their principals is inverse to the ratio of their accumulation factors: P₁/P₂ = (1 + r/100)⁽t² − t¹⁾.

Successive Percentage

Compounding annually is a form of **successive percentage increase** where the base changes every year.
